bib.title: Depth Anything: Unleashing the Power of Large-Scale Unlabeled Data

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Depth Anything: Unleashing the Power of Large-Scale Unlabeled Data", Lihe Yang, Bingyi Kang, Zilong Huang, Xiaogang Xu, Jiashi Feng, Hengshuang Zhao (HKU, TikTok, CUHK, ZJU). The PDF states no venue, only the stamp "arXiv:2401.10891v2 [cs.CV] 7 Apr 2024", so cite it as a preprint unless the venue is confirmed elsewhere.

COVERAGE: 18 of 18 pages; 59,451 of 59,451 chars (count includes my page markers). This covers the main paper (pp.1-8), the supplement (pp.9-15) and the references (pp.16-18). Nothing was skipped. Figures were identified from captions only and I did not view the images.

Quotes are verbatim, except that I joined line wraps and end-of-line hyphens. Table rows are copied as extracted.

CLAIMS

- claim: Training uses far more pseudo-labeled than labeled data, with eight unlabeled sets and six labeled sets.
  number: 1.5M labeled, 62M unlabeled
  setup: Labeled sets are BlendedMVS, DIML, HRWSI, IRS, MegaDepth, TartanAir. Unlabeled sets are BDD100K, Google Landmarks, ImageNet-21K, LSUN, Objects365, Open Images V7, Places365, SA-1B. NYUv2 and KITTI are excluded so they stay zero-shot.
  quote: "In total, our Depth Anything is trained on 1.5M labeled images and 62M unlabeled images jointly."
  where: p3, Table 1

- claim: Adding pseudo-labeled images alone gives no consistent gain; strong perturbations and then feature alignment produce the gain.
  number: AbsRel on KITTI/NYU/Sintel/DDAD/ETH3D/DIODE, from baseline to full method
  setup: ViT-L, zero-shot. Rows are cumulative: Ll; +Lu; +S; +Lfeat. Only AbsRel is reported. Column ticks collapsed in extraction, so the row order is inferred from the caption and prose.
  quote: "0.085 0.053 0.492 0.245 0.134 0.070" / "0.085 0.054 0.481 0.242 0.138 0.073" / "0.081 0.048 0.469 0.235 0.134 0.068" / "0.076 0.043 0.458 0.230 0.127 0.066"
  where: p8, Table 9

- claim: With the same mechanism, plain self-training failed in pilot studies, and the authors conjecture why.
  number: none
  setup: Teacher and student share pre-training and architecture, and labeled data is already sufficient.
  quote: "they tend to make similar correct or false predictions on the unlabeled set"
  where: p4

- claim: The ViT-L model beats the best MiDaS on all six unseen datasets, on both metrics, in zero-shot relative depth.
  number: e.g. KITTI AbsRel 0.127 to 0.076, δ1 0.850 to 0.947; DDAD AbsRel 0.251 to 0.230, δ1 0.766 to 0.789
  setup: Baseline is MiDaS v3.1 DPT-BEiTL-512. MiDaS trained on KITTI and NYUv2 images; Depth Anything did not. Scale and shift of predictions are manually aligned to ground truth (p9), and evaluation is at original resolution.
  quote: "MiDaS v3.1 [5] ViT-L 0.127 0.850 0.048 0.980 0.587 0.699 0.251 0.766 0.139 0.867 0.075 0.942" / "ViT-L 0.076 0.947 0.043 0.981 0.458 0.760 0.230 0.789 0.127 0.882 0.066 0.952"
  where: p5, Table 2

- claim: Smaller encoders stay competitive, and ViT-S is under a tenth of the MiDaS model's size.
  number: ViT-S 24.8M, ViT-B 97.5M, ViT-L 335.3M
  setup: Same zero-shot table. The student sizes all learn from pseudo-labels made by the ViT-L teacher (p5).
  quote: "ViT-S (24.8M), ViT-B (97.5M), and ViT-L (335.3M)"; "ViT-S 0.080 0.936 0.053 0.972 0.464 0.739 0.247 0.768 0.127 0.885 0.076 0.939"; "ViT-B 0.080 0.939 0.046 0.979 0.432 0.756 0.232 0.786 0.126 0.884 0.069 0.946"
  where: p5, Table 2

- claim: Among single training sets, the smallest one (HRWSI) generalizes best on the mean, which the authors read as diversity mattering.
  number: HRWSI mean AbsRel 0.200, δ1 0.846 from 20K images; all labeled data 0.180, 0.874
  setup: ViT-L, relative depth, trained on one set and tested on the six unseen sets.
  quote: "HRWSI [68] 0.095 0.917 0.062 0.966 0.502 0.731 0.270 0.750 0.186 0.775 0.087 0.935 0.200 0.846"; "All labeled data 0.085 0.934 0.053 0.971 0.492 0.748 0.245 0.771 0.134 0.874 0.070 0.945 0.180 0.874"; "even though it only contains 20K images"
  where: p7, Table 6

- claim: In-domain metric depth on NYUv2 beats the previous best.
  number: δ1 0.964 to 0.984; AbsRel 0.069 to 0.056
  setup: ViT-L encoder fine-tuned inside the ZoeDepth framework, decoder randomly initialized, 392×518, batch 16, 5 epochs, encoder LR 1/50 of decoder LR. Baseline is VPD; the ZoeDepth row is reproduced by the authors, and other rows are not stated to be.
  quote: "Ours 0.984 0.998 1.000 0.056 0.206 0.024"; "VPD [87] 0.964 0.995 0.999 0.069 0.254 0.030"
  where: p6, Table 3; p9 for setup

- claim: In-domain metric depth on KITTI also leads, by a smaller margin.
  number: δ1 0.978 to 0.982; AbsRel 0.046; RMSE 1.896
  setup: As above at 384×768. Best prior δ1 is NDDepth.
  quote: "Ours 0.982 0.998 1.000 0.046 1.896 0.069"; "NDDepth [54] 0.978 0.998 0.999 0.050 2.025 0.075"
  where: p6, Table 4

- claim: Swapping the encoder inside ZoeDepth improves zero-shot metric depth, but absolute errors stay large on some sets.
  number: order is SUN RGB-D, iBims-1, HyperSim, Virtual KITTI 2, DIODE Outdoor (AbsRel, δ1)
  setup: NYUv2-trained model for the indoor sets, KITTI-trained for the outdoor sets. ZoeDepth was reproduced in the authors' environment.
  quote: "ZoeDepth [4] 0.520 0.545 0.169 0.656 0.407 0.302 0.106 0.844 0.814 0.237"; "Depth Anything 0.500 0.660 0.150 0.714 0.363 0.361 0.085 0.913 0.794 0.288"
  where: p7, Table 5

- claim: The depth-trained encoder transfers to semantic segmentation better than the compared encoders.
  number: Cityscapes 84.8 single-scale, 86.2 multi-scale (prior best 83.6 / 84.6); ADE20K 59.4 (prior best 58.3)
  setup: ViT-L with Mask2Former, 896×896, encoder LR 3e-6, batch 16, 80K iterations on Cityscapes and 160K on ADE20K, no COCO or Mapillary pre-training.
  quote: "Ours ViT-L [16] 84.8 86.2"; "OneFormer [24] ConvNeXt-XL [41] 83.6 84.6"; "Ours ViT-L [16] 59.4"; "ViT-Adapter [11] BEiT-L [2] 58.3"
  where: p7, Tables 7-8; p9 for setup

- claim: The encoder beats both the MiDaS encoder and the original DINOv2 encoder when fine-tuned downstream.
  number: vs DINOv2, NYUv2 AbsRel 0.066 to 0.056; ADE20K mIoU 58.8 to 59.4. vs MiDaS, ADE20K 52.4 to 59.4
  setup: Columns are NYUv2 AbsRel/δ1, KITTI AbsRel/δ1, then mIoU. The MiDaS depth values in Table 10 equal the ZoeDepth* rows of Tables 3-4.
  quote: "MiDaS 0.077 0.951 0.054 0.971 82.1 52.4"; "Ours 0.056 0.984 0.046 0.982 84.8 59.4"; "DINOv2 0.066 0.973 0.058 0.971 58.8"
  where: p8, Tables 10-11

- claim: Feature alignment needs a tolerance margin, because forcing full alignment hurts part-level depth discrimination.
  number: mean AbsRel 0.188 (α=1.00), 0.175 (α=0.85), 0.178 (α=0.70)
  setup: ViT-S, six unseen sets. Pixels with cosine similarity above α are dropped from Lfeat.
  quote: "1.00 0.085 0.055 0.523 0.250 0.134 0.079 0.188"; "0.85 0.080 0.053 0.464 0.247 0.127 0.076 0.175"; "0.70 0.079 0.054 0.482 0.248 0.127 0.077 0.178"
  where: p9, Table 12

- claim: Applying feature alignment to labeled data gives no benefit; it helps on unlabeled data.
  number: mean AbsRel 0.180 none, 0.175 unlabeled, 0.179 labeled
  setup: ViT-S. The authors conjecture that it interferes with informative manual labels but combats noise in pseudo-labels.
  quote: "their mean AbsRel values are almost the same: 0.180 vs. 0.179"
  where: p9, Table 13

- claim: An auxiliary discrete segmentation task did not improve depth, which motivated aligning to continuous DINOv2 features instead.
  number: 4K classes
  setup: Labels came from RAM + GroundingDINO + HQ-SAM, with a shared encoder and two decoders. No metric table is given for this failed attempt.
  quote: "this yields a class space containing 4K classes"
  where: p4

- claim: The training recipe is a two-stage teacher then student, with a fresh student rather than fine-tuning from the teacher.
  number: 20 teacher epochs; one sweep of unlabeled data; labeled:unlabeled 1:2 per batch; encoder LR 5e-6, decoder 10× larger; α 0.85; CutMix 50%
  setup: AdamW with linear decay. DINOv2 encoder and DPT decoder. Labeled images get horizontal flip only. Unlabeled images get color jitter, Gaussian blur and CutMix; the teacher sees clean images. Overall loss is the average of Ll, Lu, Lfeat. Sky disparity is set to 0 using a segmentation model.
  quote: "we train a teacher model on labeled images for 20 epochs"; "The ratio of labeled and unlabeled images is set as 1:2 in each batch"; "the base learning rate of the pre-trained encoder is set as 5e-6"; "The tolerance margin α for feature alignment loss is set as 0.85"; "We use CutMix with 50% probability"
  where: p5; p4 for CutMix

- claim: Image handling depends on DINOv2's patch size.
  number: 518 training crop; patch size 14
  setup: At inference, images are not cropped but both sides must be multiples of 14.
  quote: "All images are cropped to 518 ×518 during training."; "the pre-defined patch size of DINOv2 encoders [43] is 14"
  where: p9

- claim: The metrics are defined explicitly.
  number: δ1 threshold 1.25
  setup: Applies to all depth tables.
  quote: "AbsRel (absolute relative error: |d∗ − d|/d) and δ1 (percentage of max(d∗/d, d/d∗) < 1.25)"
  where: p5

LIMITS

Conceded by the authors (p9, section 8):
- The largest model is ViT-L, and ViT-Giant is planned.
- Quote: "the widely adopted 512×512 training resolution is not enough". They plan 700+ or 1000+.
- In-domain metric results use "a relatively basic depth model" (p6).

Not shown in the source:
- No latency, FPS or memory figures. Model parameter counts are the only size evidence, so the "computationally-constrained" claim (p5) is not measured.
- No seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. Many gains are in the second or third decimal.
- Pseudo-label quality is never measured directly.
- There is no scaling curve of accuracy against the number of unlabeled images, and no per-dataset unlabeled ablation.
- The ControlNet and video editing claims are qualitative only (Figure 4, p8; project page).
- Zero-shot relative results are aligned to ground truth for scale and shift, so they do not show metric accuracy.
- Failed attempts (naive self-training, discrete segmentation) are described without numbers beyond Table 9.
- Reasons are stated as conjecture or speculation ("We conjecture", "We speculate"). They are not tested.

Comparability:
- Table 3 and Table 4 baselines other than ZoeDepth are not marked as reproduced, so they are not confirmed to come from one environment.
- The Cityscapes prose compares multi-scale figures (86.2, 84.3, 84.6), but Table 10 uses single-scale 84.8.

Prose stronger than its tables (my reading of the tables):
- "ViT-B ... clearly superior" to MiDaS: on NYUv2 δ1 ViT-B is 0.979 against MiDaS 0.980.
- ViT-S loses to MiDaS on NYUv2 (both metrics) and on DIODE (both metrics).
- ViT-L is not the best size everywhere. Sintel AbsRel is best at ViT-B (0.432), ETH3D AbsRel at ViT-B (0.126), ETH3D δ1 at ViT-S (0.885).
- Table 9 row 2 is worse than baseline on NYU, ETH3D and DIODE, better on Sintel and DDAD, and tied on KITTI.
- Across Tables 12-13, α=1.00 (0.188) is worse than no alignment at all (0.180). The paper compares only 1.00 with 0.85 and 0.70.

Possibly dated: comparisons are to baselines as of the arXiv date, and section 8 plans a later higher-resolution, larger model. The PDF contains no information on later versions.

BUILDS ON (as printed)
- Affine-invariant loss and multi-dataset training: MiDaS, Ranftl et al., TPAMI 2020 [46]; MiDaS v3.1, Birkl et al., arXiv 2023 [5].
- Encoder: DINOv2, Oquab et al., TMLR 2023 [43]; ViT, Dosovitskiy et al., ICLR 2021 [16].
- Decoder: DPT, Ranftl et al., ICCV 2021 [47].
- Metric fine-tuning codebase: ZoeDepth, Bhat et al., arXiv 2023 [4].
- Self-training: Pseudo-label, Lee, ICMLW 2013 [31]; re-initializing the student, ST++, Yang et al., CVPR 2022 [74]; few-label contrast, FixMatch, Sohn et al., NeurIPS 2020 [56]; Yalniz et al., arXiv 2019 [73]; Zoph et al., NeurIPS 2020 [90].
- Perturbation: CutMix, Yun et al., ICCV 2019 [84].
- Semantic auxiliary line: Chen et al., CVPR 2019 [9]; Guizilini et al., ICLR 2020 [21]; Klingner et al., ECCV 2020 [28]; Xu et al., ECCV 2022 [72].
- Projector design it declines to follow: BYOL, Grill et al., NeurIPS 2020 [19].
- Naming and data: Segment Anything, Kirillov et al., ICCV 2023 [27].
- Foundation models framing: Bommasani et al., arXiv 2021 [6].
- Early deep MDE: Eigen et al., NeurIPS 2014 [17].
- Sky mask: SegFormer, Xie et al., NeurIPS 2021 [70].
- Conditioning demo: ControlNet, Zhang et al., ICCV 2023 [85].
- Segmentation head and codebase: Mask2Former, Cheng et al., CVPR 2022 [12]; MMSegmentation 2020 [14].

CODE: None in the PDF, and no repository URL beyond https://depth-anything.github.io (p1). The key equations are on p3 (Eq. 1-3 affine-invariant loss), p4 (Eq. 5-8 CutMix loss) and p5 (Eq. 9 Lfeat). Their extraction is garbled, so transcribe them from the PDF rather than from this text. One equation fragment extracted cleanly: "uab = ua ⊙ M + ub ⊙ (1 − M )," (p4, Eq. 5).

FIGURES
- Figure 2, p4: "Our pipeline. Solid line: flow of labeled images, dotted line: unlabeled images." The best candidate. It shows teacher, pseudo-labels, strong perturbation and frozen-encoder alignment in one diagram.
- Figure 1, p1: predictions across COCO, SA-1B and the authors' own photos, in low light, fog and at long distance. Useful for showing what generalization looks like.
- Figure 4, p8: depth compared with MiDaS, plus ControlNet synthesis from each depth map. Shows depth as a conditioning signal for generation.
- Figure 3, p8: "Qualitative results on six unseen datasets." A compact overview.
- Figures 5-10, pp.10-15: input, ours and MiDaS v3.1 side by side, on KITTI, NYUv2, Sintel, DDAD, ETH3D and DIODE. Figure 5 explains that sparse KITTI ground truth is hard to visualize; brighter means closer. Figure 6 notes MiDaS used NYUv2 training data.

PROBLEMS
- No embedded instructions were found.
- Extraction faults: equations are garbled, table highlighting (best and second best) is lost, and tick marks in Tables 9 and 13 have lost their columns. Table 13's row meaning is confirmed by the prose. Table 9's is inferred.
- Table 1 does not sum to the headline for labeled data: its rows total 1,599K (about 1.6M), while the text says 1.5M. Unlabeled rows total 62.3M, consistent with "more than 62M" (my arithmetic).
- Table 2 labels the MiDaS row "ViT-L" while the text calls it "DPT-BEiTL-512" (p5). Figure 1 calls SA-1B "a hold-out unseen set" although Table 1 lists SA-1B as an 11.1M training source. The PDF does not explain how the split works.
- The spellings "Ablation", "fine-tuning" and "zero-shot" are as extracted. Check them against the PDF if quoting in a note.
